Infinite Latin Squares

CountingAlgorithmsInvariants
Game: Fill an endless grid so every row and column uses each number exactly once.
How to play: Change the size to see bigger corners of the infinite square, or colour the numbers.
Look for the math

An infinite grid can be filled so that every row and every column contains every whole number exactly once. The rule is simpler than it looks.

Write the numbers in binary

Put i XOR j in row i, column j, where XOR is bitwise exclusive or. In binary, XOR adds without carrying. Doubling the corner square copies it into three quarters and adds the new high bit to two of them — exactly the rule the applet uses. The number 0, 1, 2, …, 7 in binary is 000 through 111, and adding 4 prepends a 1 to each.

Why it never repeats

Every corner of side 2ⁿ is a finite Latin square: XOR with a fixed number is a one-to-one map, so each row and column contains each symbol once. Since every cell lies in some finite corner, the whole quadrant is Latin. The logic test checks the doubling construction against the XOR formula and confirms the Latin property for all seven levels.

Set the modulus to 4 and look at the repeating colour pattern. What do you notice?
